title: All three Executor Agents operate with their Artifacts deferred to a future Atlas iteration
content:
A.6.1.2.1, A.6.1.2.2 and A.6.1.2.3 use near-identical language: the Agent Artifact "will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas," and "in the interim, the subdocuments herein contain key information."

What those subdocuments contain is only two facts per Agent — who the Facilitator is and who holds GovOps. So every Executor Agent is currently live with **no published rules, processes or parameters** governing its operations, despite A.6.1.2 defining Executor Agent Artifacts as precisely the documents that should contain them.

This is a governance gap rather than a contradiction: the Atlas is explicit that the specification is pending. But it means the Agent Scope's claim to "regulate all Agents" (A.6) is, for Executor Agents, currently satisfied by an assignment of responsible parties rather than by any rule an outsider could check compliance against.
description: Amatsu, Ozone and Core Council Executor Agent 1 each state their Artifact 'will be specified in a future iteration', leaving only Facilitator and GovOps assignments as interim governance.
